mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decline over the past month is followed by negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 9.0% over the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 9.0%, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC over 2-year window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic contraction that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO is followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 215.0), a rise in the federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases the discount rate for equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 215.0, a rise in FEDFUNDS is followed by positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC over 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month signals weakening manufacturing activity that reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline over the past month is followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC over 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 590.0 thousand units over the past month signals reduced consumer confidence in the housing market, which dampens overall economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 590.0, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC over 2-year window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a weakening consumer sector that reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST and rise in UNRATE is followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong economic growth (GDPC1 > 13200.0), a rise in retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer spending that boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 13200.0, a rise in RSAFS is followed by negative 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC over 3-year window is below 0.03.
